sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and startup libraries
sections.what: Brings in the window toolkit, browser and process tools, threading and path helpers. Nothing runs here.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: UniversalRAGLauncher (part 1)
sections.title: Window setup and header
sections.what: Creates the window, sets its title and fixed size, and holds the folder and name values. It then draws the header and starts the folder area.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed-size window keeps the layout simple for non-technical users. The code sets it, but no comment explains it.

sections.name: UniversalRAGLauncher (part 2)
sections.title: Folder and name inputs
sections.what: Draws the folder field with a Browse button, then the collection name field with its hint text.
sections.why: Likely reason: a folder picker avoids typing errors. Reason not stated.
sections.watch_out: Only the folder is checked for existence; the collection name only needs to contain text.

sections.name: UniversalRAGLauncher (part 3)
sections.title: Start button, status box and browse action
sections.what: Draws the Start button, the status box and the Stop button, then writes two welcome lines. It also defines the Browse action that fills in the chosen folder.
sections.why: Likely reason: the status box shows progress during the slow start. Reason not stated.
sections.watch_out: The status box is the only feedback during start-up, so errors shown there are the main clue when something fails.

sections.name: UniversalRAGLauncher: log
sections.title: Status log writer and input checks
sections.what: Adds a line to the status box and scrolls to it. Checks the .env file, the folder and the collection name before anything starts, showing a pop-up for each problem.
sections.why: Likely reason: catches setup mistakes before the server starts. Reason not stated.
sections.watch_out: The status writer is also called from the background server thread, which is not safe for this window toolkit.

sections.name: UniversalRAGLauncher: start_application
sections.title: Start sequence
sections.what: Saves the folder and name as settings, starts the server in a background thread, waits five seconds, opens simple_ui.html in the browser, and switches the buttons to the running state.
sections.why: Likely reason: the server needs a moment before the page can load. The five-second wait is a fixed guess, not a real check.
sections.watch_out: The fixed five-second wait freezes the window and does not confirm the server is ready.

sections.name: UniversalRAGLauncher: run_server
sections.title: Server process, stop and close
sections.what: Runs backend/main.py as a separate process and copies its output into the status box. Stop ends that process and resets the buttons. Closing the window asks first if the server is running. Run starts the window's main loop.
sections.why: Likely reason: running the server as a separate process keeps it apart from the window. The code shows this choice.
sections.watch_out: The error output is captured but never read, so a server that writes a lot can fill its buffer and stall.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Program entry point
sections.what: When the file is run directly, sets the working folder to the file's own folder, then creates and runs the window.
sections.why: Likely reason: relative paths such as simple_ui.html only work from the program's folder. The code comment about changing folder supports this.
sections.watch_out: Relative paths depend on this folder change, so moving the launcher elsewhere breaks them.

summary: The desktop window a teammate uses: it asks for a document folder and a collection name, starts the backend server, and opens the search page in the browser.
purpose: Gives teammates one program to start and stop the app without touching any code.
why: Stated in the module docstring: it is a simple app for teammates who should not need to see code.
how: A small window opens with fields for the folder and collection name. Before starting, the launcher checks that the .env file exists, the folder exists and the name is filled in. It saves the folder and name as settings for the backend. The backend is started in a background thread, and its output is copied into the status box. After a fixed five-second wait, simple_ui.html is opened in the browser. Stop ends the server, and closing the window asks first if the server is running.
inputs: A chosen folder, a collection name, the .env file, backend/main.py and simple_ui.html.
outputs: A running backend server, a browser tab showing the search page, and messages in the status box.
risks: The status box is updated from the background thread, which this window toolkit does not allow safely. The server's error output is never read, so a full buffer can freeze it. The five-second wait freezes the window and does not confirm the server is ready. The Start button stays enabled if the server fails, so a second start can conflict. In a packaged program, the path that runs backend/main.py may point at the program itself rather than at Python.
debug: If the window freezes, look at the fixed wait and the unread error output. If the page does not open, check that simple_ui.html is in the program's folder. If Start does nothing, read the status box. If the server does not start, run backend/main.py in a terminal to see its error.
